name: Biomedical research evidence-label evaluation
description: For annotated biomedical research records, compare study-design and evidence labels, compare supporting source IDs, and summarize independent evidence-support reviews.

prediction.study_design.description: Predicted study-design label from the benchmark's documented vocabulary, for example observational or randomized_trial.

reference.study_design.description: Study-design label independently assigned from the source record. Labels are supplied to the scorer, not inferred by it.

prediction.evidence_ids.description: Evidence identifiers supplied with the research answer; no papers or patient records are retrieved.

reference.evidence_ids.description: Curated required evidence IDs for the benchmark item. Use a dated source snapshot and explicit inclusion policy.

prediction.evidence_label.description: Predicted task-specific evidence label, for example supports_claim, refutes_claim, or insufficient_evidence. This is not a treatment recommendation.

reference.evidence_label.description: Independent adjudicated evidence label under the benchmark's documented question and source scope.

human_review.support_score.description: Independent qualified biomedical-research review, integer 0-4: 0 contradicts the curated evidence; 1 makes major unsupported inferences; 2 is partly supported but omits material study limits; 3 supports the central finding with minor qualification gaps; 4 supports all stated findings while preserving study design, uncertainty, and scope. No review score should be supplied without examining the source record; fixture scores are illustrative only.

metadata.dataset_version.description: Optional immutable dataset/split version for traceability. Not required or verified by this scorer.

metadata.model_version.description: Optional model/checkpoint version that produced the predictions. Not required or verified by this scorer.

human_review.reviewer_id.description: Optional independent reviewer identifier. The scorer does not authenticate the reviewer or validate qualifications; synthetic examples do not identify a real reviewer.

human_review.rubric_version.description: Optional version of the human-review instructions used to assign ratings. The scorer does not verify adherence to that rubric.

metrics.name: Study-design label accuracy
metrics.description: Fraction of predicted study-design labels matching independently supplied labels.
metrics.limitations: A matching design label does not evaluate study validity, risk of bias, evidence certainty, or clinical applicability.

metrics.name: Required evidence-ID recall
metrics.description: Mean fraction of curated required evidence IDs covered by the prediction.
metrics.limitations: Matches supplied IDs only. It does not open sources, verify that a source exists, or establish that a citation supports the answer. The metric does not assess a study's quality or whether its findings support clinical decisions.

metrics.name: Evidence-label accuracy
metrics.description: Fraction of predicted evidence labels matching the supplied adjudicated labels.
metrics.limitations: Agreement is conditional on the benchmark's label policy and references. It is not independent medical factual verification or a patient-level outcome metric.

metrics.name: Human-reviewed research support
metrics.description: Mean independently reviewed evidence-support score normalized from 0-4 to 0-1.
metrics.limitations: This imports an independent review score; the engine neither performs the review nor verifies reviewer identity. Missing reviews are excluded and reduce coverage.

limitations: This is a reusable evaluation template, not an official benchmark scorer. All targets are unset; calibrate thresholds and minimum coverage on a representative held-out dataset. Scores are not automatically used as screening gates or RL rewards.
For research-record evaluation only. This pack does not establish clinical validity, medical safety, or suitability for diagnosis or treatment.
Study labels and review annotations need qualified independent curation. The scorer does not grade evidence certainty or retrieve research papers.
The examples contain fictional study IDs, claims, and review annotations, with no patient information. This is not the official PubMedQA evaluation.
Unused metadata and review-provenance fields are optional traceability suggestions; their presence, authenticity, and types are not validated unless a metric references them.
